Its bytes are the seed of one channel,
and a pass carries at most one adapter.
one reader, shared by the Metal, CUDA, XLA and GPU engines
Parse the safetensors header. Each tensor must lie
inside the file, fill its shape exactly, and be
The same bytes always give the same key.
Match each tensor to the registered bank of the
same name, cast it to the bank's type (bf16 or
f32), and on a tensor-parallel rank cut it to
that rank's share. One slot-sized plane each.
A failed check in step 1 or 3 refuses the whole bundle,
naming the tensor (“is not a registered bank of this deployment”).
(c) Metal binds it to one slot
Slots::acquire(key), then at most one write
Is the key held by a running pass?
Is the key kept by a released slot?
take that slot back, no write
Is a slot free, or kept by another key?
Every slot is held by a running pass
(a free slot first, else the one kept longest)
Registered banks of layer ℓ, one slot per row
(LoRA mounted on every site; this bundle trains q and v)
zeroed: the bundle does not name it
Zeroing means a slot never keeps what an earlier adapter wrote into it.
The pass then runs with slot 2, and the adapted rows read their banks at slot 2.
Figure 1. Serving an adapter bundle by bank name (#1711). A pass attaches a safetensors bundle (a). The reader every engine shares checks it, keys it by its bytes
and turns each tensor into a plane for the bank of the same name (b). Metal writes each distinct bundle into one slot once, zeroing the banks the bundle does not name (c).
